mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 7.0% signals strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in >55% of instances when UNRATE < 7.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in residential construction (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand that accelerates corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns negative in >55% of periods when HOUST and RSAFS both rise, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 100.5 index points during late-cycle expansion indicates manufacturing capacity growth that supports corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns negative in >55% of periods when INDPRO > 100.5 during late-cycle, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising residential construction permits (HOUST) signal increasing housing market activity that boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns negative in >55% of periods when HOUST rises, or Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate above 3.0% signals restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns positive in >55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment decline (UNRATE) indicates labor market strength that increases disposable income and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns negative in >55% of periods when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized) during high inflation periods triggers expected Fed rate hikes that increase equity discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns positive in >55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03.
